name: Orzo salad with roasted kabocha, chickpeas, kale, and feta
time: 45 minutes, most of it roasting and cooling
yield: Six snack bowls, or four lunches
intro: Make it on Sunday and it carries the week: orzo and chickpeas dressed while the orzo is hot, dark-roasted squash, lacinato kale rubbed soft with the dressing, salty feta. Pomegranate goes on each bowl as you eat it.
needs: ½ large kabocha (about 1½ lbs), in ¾-inch cubes
1 bunch lacinato kale, leaves stripped from the ribs and sliced thin
⅓ cup olive oil, plus more for the squash

steps.text: Heat the oven. Toss the squash with oil and salt, spread it on a sheet pan in one layer, and roast, flipping once, until the edges are dark and it's tender. Let it cool.
Whisk the olive oil, vinegar, lemon juice, garlic, a pinch of chile flakes, and ½ tsp salt in a large bowl. Spoon 2 tbsp of it into a small jar and keep it for serving.
Put the kale in a second bowl with a pinch of salt and 1 tbsp of the dressing, and squeeze it with your hands for a minute, until it darkens and softens. Set it aside.
Boil the orzo in well-salted water — it should taste like the sea — for 2 minutes longer than the package says. Cold pasta firms up, so it needs the extra time.
Drain it without rinsing and toss it hot with the chickpeas and the dressing in the bowl. Hot pasta drinks the dressing; cold pasta only gets coated.
Spread the dressed orzo on a sheet pan to cool so it doesn't clump.
Fold in the cooled squash, the kale, and the feta, pack it into a covered container, and refrigerate it within 2 hours. Keep the pomegranate out.
Scoop a bowl, add some pomegranate and a spoonful of the saved dressing, and taste: cold dulls flavor, so it usually wants a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt.

how_it_works: Three things make a pasta salad last: dress the pasta while it's hot so the flavor goes in, not just on; cook it a little past al dente because the cold firms it; and keep anything delicate out of the container until you eat it. Kale is the one green that belongs in the container: rubbed with salt and dressing, it softens without wilting. Chickpeas soak up the dressing alongside the orzo and give every bite something to bite into. The formula works every month — orzo, the month's vegetable, one cheese, a sharp dressing, something fresh at the end.
swaps: Leftover roasted sweet potato in place of the kabocha.
Whisk a spoonful of ajvar into the dressing for smoke.
Torn dates for sweetness against the feta.
leftovers: It is the leftovers. Covered in the fridge, it keeps 3 to 4 days. The kale is at its best for the first two, then softens more, like a cooked green.

make_it_a_meal: For a lunch, halve two soft-boiled eggs over the bowl and crumble on a little more feta. The yolks dress the orzo.

nutrition.serving: A lunch: a quarter of the salad, with pomegranate on top. As one of six snack bowls, about two-thirds of these numbers.
